product: Health Triage: a health-guidance mobile app whose backend takes symptoms, voice notes and medical documents, runs an asynchronous AI triage pipeline (speech-to-text, OCR, Gemini), and sells monthly plans and one-time top-ups through Google Play and the App Store.
stack: Redis (rate limits, OTP, pub/sub, Celery broker)
Google Play Billing + App Store Server API
architecture: The Flutter app calls https://api.../api/v1 through nginx (TLS termination, forwarded headers, a no-buffering location for SSE), which proxies to three gunicorn/uvicorn workers running one FastAPI app. Requests pass RequestId, TrustedHost, CORS and SecurityHeaders middleware, then per-route dependencies (JWT + session lookup, plan entitlements, Redis fixed-window rate limits). Handlers talk to MongoDB directly through module-level Motor collections; billing logic sits in a service module. Slow work (speech-to-text, OCR, Gemini triage and final analysis, vision, push notifications) is enqueued to Celery over Redis and executed by a 16-thread worker using sync PyMongo/Redis clients; progress is written to the assessment document and published on Redis pub/sub, which the API relays to the client as Server-Sent Events with polling as fallback. Files go client to S3 via presigned URLs. Google Play (Pub/Sub push) and Apple (signed JWS) webhooks update subscriptions idempotently, with an hourly reconcile job as backstop. Everything runs as docker compose services (nginx, certbot, api, worker, beat) on a single EC2 host, deployed by a GitHub Actions workflow that builds, pushes and SSHes in; logs go to CloudWatch and errors to Sentry. NOTE: the evidence entries in this file are re-mapped from the backend edition (bfp-annotated) to the AI Engineering chapters; there is no local copy of the repo, so the lines and snippets could not be re-verified locally for this edition.

evidence.concept: Two-stage LLM workflow with a human answer in between
evidence.what: Stage one (triage) produces an internal assessment and 2-3 questions and parks the job in awaiting_answers; the user's answers trigger stage two.
evidence.lesson: A fixed sequential workflow, not an agent loop: no tool calling and no model-chosen next step.

evidence.concept: Validating model output before trusting it
evidence.what: The triage response must parse as JSON and contain questions, otherwise the task fails and is retried.
evidence.lesson: The final analysis is stored unvalidated as rawMarkdown and parsed at read time with a fallback.

evidence.concept: Guardrail: the model must classify the image as medical first
evidence.snippet:

evidence.concept: Prompt-level constraints
evidence.snippet:
CONSTRAINTS:
- Return ONLY JSON. No markdown, no backticks, no extra text.
- The "is_medical" field is REQUIRED and must be a boolean.
- If is_medical is false, DO NOT include any analysis fields (no observations, no interpretations, no next_steps).
- If is_medical is true, ALL accepted-schema fields are REQUIRED.
- Never "try to be helpful" with non-medical images. Reject them.
evidence.what: The prompt fixes the output contract (JSON only, required boolean, no analysis when rejecting).

evidence.concept: Cost and safety controls around the model
evidence.snippet:
gemini_limit = RedisRateLimiterSync(
    key_prefix="gemini",
    limit=GEMINI_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN,
    window=60
)
evidence.what: A global per-minute limiter, per-plan quotas, kill switches and a queue-depth gate sit in front of every model call.
evidence.lesson: No evals or recorded prompts to detect quality regressions.

evidence.concept: Dependency injection: auth result feeds a per-user limiter
evidence.snippet:
def per_api_rate_limit(limit: int, window: int = 60):
    limiter = RedisRateLimiter(
        key_prefix="endpoint",
        limit=limit,
        window=window
    )
    async def dependency(
        request: Request,
        user=Depends(auth_required)
    ):
        identifier = f"{user['_id']}:{request.url.path}"
        await limiter.check(identifier)
    return dependency
evidence.what: per_api_rate_limit is a factory that returns a dependency; that dependency itself depends on auth_required and keys the limiter by user id + path.
evidence.lesson: auth_required is resolved once per request by FastAPI's dependency cache, which is what keeps this cheap.

evidence.concept: Global rate limit inside workers with spaced retries
evidence.what: Before calling Gemini the task reserves a slot on a shared Redis limiter; if saturated it retries after 30s and, once retries run out, raises a typed error so the caller can mark the job failed.

evidence.concept: Back-pressure: reject new work when queues are deep
evidence.snippet:
ingest_depth = await r.llen(f"{Q}ingest")
    ai_depth = await r.llen(f"{Q}ai")
    if max(ingest_depth, ai_depth) > features.max_queue_depth:
        raise HTTPException(429, "System is busy. Try again later.")
evidence.what: Before enqueuing, the API reads the Redis list length of both queues and returns 429 if it exceeds an admin-configurable max_queue_depth.

evidence.concept: One quick retry with jitter for transient model errors
evidence.what: Only 503/429/connection errors are retried, once, after 1-2s of jittered sleep; longer backoff is left to Celery's task-level retry.

evidence.concept: Circuit breaker written but never used
evidence.what: A Redis-backed CircuitBreaker class exists (failure counter, open-until timestamp) but nothing imports it, so a provider outage is absorbed only by retries and rate limits.
evidence.lesson: Wrap _call_gemini and the Sarvam call with it, or delete it.

evidence.concept: Graceful degradation switches
evidence.what: With the AI flag off or kill switch on, assessments are still accepted and ingested; only the AI stage is skipped.

evidence.concept: Consumer with automatic retry and backoff
evidence.what: triage_task is a bound Celery task that retries any exception up to 3 times with exponential backoff starting at 10s.
evidence.lesson: autoretry_for=(Exception,) also retries permanent errors such as invalid JSON from the model.

evidence.concept: Producer: mark queued atomically, then enqueue
evidence.snippet:
res = await assessments.update_one(
                {"_id": ObjectId(assessment_id), "processing.stt": {"$nin": ["queued", "running"]}},
                {"$set": {"processing.stt": "queued", "processing.sttUpdatedAt": now_utc()}},

            if res.modified_count:

                tasks_triggered.append("stt")
                stt_queued = True
evidence.what: The handler flips processing.stt to queued only if not already queued/running and enqueues the Celery task only when that update matched.

evidence.concept: Chained stages: ingest fans in to triage
evidence.snippet:

    res = assessments.update_one(

        {"$set": {"processing.triage": "queued", "processing.triageUpdatedAt": now_utc()}},

            assessment=fresh,

evidence.concept: Compensation: refund the credit when the job fails for good
evidence.what: When retries are exhausted the worker refunds the usage credit, routed by the assessment id to the bucket it was charged from.

evidence.concept: Service layer for quota logic
evidence.snippet:
if limit > 0:
        _res = await _charge_plan_counter(user_id, period, metric, limit, now)
        if _res:
            await _record_charge_source(ref_id, user_id, metric, "plan", now)
            return
    # Plan quota exhausted (or zero) for this cycle. Draw from the durable top-up
    # balance (reserve). Only metrics in _TOPUP_METRICS have balances.
    if await _try_consume_topup(user_id, metric):
        await _record_charge_source(ref_id, user_id, metric, "topup", now)
        return
    # No plan quota and no top-up balance → genuinely over limit.
    raise HTTPException(403, f"{metric} limit exceeded")
evidence.what: check_and_increment_usage owns the business rule 'spend plan quota first, then top-up balance, else 403'; routes just call it.
evidence.lesson: The service raises HTTPException, coupling it to the web layer (workers have to catch HTTPException from the limiter for the same reason).

evidence.concept: Durable ledger separate from the subscription record
evidence.what: Top-up credits live in their own collection and are applied once per purchase token via a $ne guard.

evidence.concept: Versioned event schema for the SSE stream
evidence.snippet:
class SSEEvent(BaseModel):
    v: Literal[1] = 1
    type: SSEEventType
    assessmentId: str
    payload: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    step: Optional[int] = None
    totalSteps: Optional[int] = None
    percent: Optional[int] = Field(default=None, ge=0, le=100)
    ts: datetime
evidence.what: Every server-sent event is an SSEEvent with a version field, an enum type, optional step/percent and a timestamp; workers serialize it with .json() and the API re-validates it before forwarding.

evidence.concept: Fallback to polling when the stream fails
evidence.what: SSE is primary; on error or early close the screen starts a 3-second polling timer against /status.
evidence.lesson: No Last-Event-ID resume; the fallback re-fetches full status instead.

evidence.concept: SSE client written by hand
evidence.what: The Flutter client opens a streamed GET with Accept: text/event-stream and a Bearer header, then parses lines into events itself.

evidence.concept: Server-Sent Events endpoint
evidence.snippet:
async def gen():
        pubsub = r.pubsub(ignore_subscribe_messages=True)
        await pubsub.subscribe(channel)
        start = asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
        try:
            yield {
                "event": "update",
                "data": SSEEvent(
                    v=1,
                    type="OPEN",
                    assessmentId=assessment_id,
                    payload=None,
                    ts=now_utc(),
                ).model_dump_json()
evidence.what: An async generator subscribes to the Redis channel and yields an OPEN event, wrapped by EventSourceResponse.

evidence.concept: Stream lifecycle: forward, detect terminal event, close
evidence.what: Each message is validated and forwarded; the loop ends on a terminal event or after 5 minutes.
evidence.lesson: Each event is parsed twice, there is an extra 0.5s sleep per iteration, and each client holds its own Redis connection.

evidence.concept: Client disconnect cancels the stream and cleans up
evidence.snippet:
except asyncio.CancelledError:
            pass
        finally:
            await pubsub.unsubscribe(channel)
            await pubsub.close()
evidence.what: When the client goes away the SSE generator is cancelled; the finally block unsubscribes and closes the Redis pub/sub connection.

evidence.concept: Redis as the backplane between workers and API processes
evidence.snippet:

evidence.concept: Scrubbing sensitive keys before events leave the process
evidence.what: A recursive scrubber redacts any dict key in a deny-list (tokens, OTP, phone, purchase tokens) from Sentry payloads.
evidence.lesson: Meanwhile auth_required sets the Sentry user email and otp.py logs the recipient address.

evidence.concept: Request id accepted, generated and echoed
evidence.snippet:
incoming = request.headers.get(_HEADER)
        rid = incoming if incoming else uuid.uuid4().hex
        token = request_id_ctx.set(rid)
        with sentry_sdk.configure_scope() as scope:

evidence.concept: Propagating the request id across the task queue
evidence.what: A before_task_publish hook copies the request id into Celery message headers and task_prerun restores it into the ContextVar in the worker, so API and worker logs share one id.
